title: Automated Analysis and Prediction of Job Interview Performance
metricDefinition: Automated lexical, facial, and prosodic features predict weighted human ratings; human rubric items include speaking rate, fillers, and pause appropriateness.

study.deviceAndEnvironment: Room with desk and wall-mounted audiovisual capture

measurements.definition: Human judgment of whether speaking rate was good.
measurements.calculationMethod: Ordinal item rated by independent judges.
notes: No WPM value or boundary is defined.

measurements.definition: Human judgment of whether too many filler words were used.
measurements.calculationMethod: Ordinal item rated by independent judges.

measurements.definition: Human judgment of whether pauses were appropriate.
measurements.calculationMethod: Ordinal item rated by independent judges.

reportedFindings.summary: The framework predicts human-rated interview traits from multimodal inputs, while learned feature importance remains model-specific.
The rating questions demonstrate the need for human semantic judgment of delivery behaviors.

faceFitMappings.reason: A human appropriateness rating is not automated WPM.
Lexicon matches are only candidates and cannot reproduce human semantic review.
Human pause appropriateness is not total positive inter-word gap.
Human pause appropriateness is not the p90 of timestamp gaps.

thresholdAssessment.reason: Ratings, correlations, classification performance, and learned importance do not define behavior boundaries.

limitations: Human ratings are context-dependent and require reliability checks.
English mock-interview evidence does not validate Korean STT-derived delivery metrics.
